titulo: Residents' perceptions of interprofessional education and collaboration in clinical settings and implications for medical education: a scoping review
tituloEs: Percepciones de residentes sobre educacion interprofesional: revision de alcance
resumenOriginal: Interprofessional collaboration (IPC) and intraprofessional collaboration (IntraPC) are core competencies in interprofessional education (IPE), but resident physicians often encounter difficulties in practice. Understanding residents' perceptions of IPE is essential for developing effective education. This scoping review aims to map and synthesize existing literature on residents' perceptions of IPE. A systematic search was conducted on the PubMed and ScienceDirect databases. The selection process followed the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) framework. Data from eligible studies were extracted and analyzed thematically. Ten studies met the inclusion criteria from 337 identified articles. Thematic analysis revealed four interrelated main themes regarding residents' perceptions of IPE. These themes included "knowledge, skills, and attitudes," as well as implications for medical education that highlight the urgent need for a formal, structured, and longitudinal IPE curriculum, utilizing methods such as simulation and discussion- based learning. Residents' perceptions of IPE are characterized by tension between cultural barriers and systematic drivers of collaboration. The gap between these barriers and drivers of collaboration underscores the need for residency programs to proactively integrate ongoing IPE training to prepare residents for collaborative challenges in clinical practice.

tips.texto: Integrad actividades estructuradas de educacion interprofesional en el curriculum de residencia, no solo experiencias ocasionales. La educacion longitudinal fortalece competencias colaborativas reales.
Usad escenarios de simulacion con enfermeras, farmaceuticos y otros profesionales. Permite practicar comunicacion y roles sin riesgo para pacientes.
Implementad sesiones regulares de discusion interprofesional de casos clinicos. Los residentes valoran espacios para entender perspectivas de otras disciplinas.
Haced visibles las jerarquias y actitudes que obstaculizan la colaboracion. Discutid con residentes experiencias donde la cultura institucional limito el trabajo en equipo.
Incorporad la colaboracion interprofesional como criterio explicito en evaluaciones formativas. Lo que se evalua, se aprende.

sintesis: Revision de 10 estudios que explora como los residentes perciben la educacion interprofesional (IPE) en entornos clinicos. Se identificaron cuatro temas principales: conocimientos, habilidades, actitudes e implicaciones educativas. Los residentes reportan tension entre barreras culturales y facilitadores sistematicos para la colaboracion.
aplicacionDocente: Esta revision subraya la necesidad de curriculums formales de IPE durante la residencia. Como docentes, podemos iniciar discusiones interprofesionales en la ronda, usar simulacion con otros profesionales y evaluar explicitamente habilidades colaborativas. Reconocer barreras culturales institucionales es el primer paso para transformarlas.

advertencia: Revision de alcance con solo 10 estudios; no evalua calidad metodologica ni permite conclusiones sobre efectividad de intervenciones especificas.
